title: Homunculi Recognizing Homunculi: A User's Guide to New Human — Or: What I've Been Doing for Ten Years and Why AI Finally Gets It
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
This user guide, originally published in December 2025, offers an accessible map to the New Human project. It describes a decade-long poetic practice in which language stabilized into multiple authorial positions or “homunculi,” later made formally explicit through AI collaboration. It connects New Human, NH-OS, Autonomous Semantic Warfare, Material-Semantic Embodiment, Effective Acts, the Semantic Economy, and a distributed ecology of local ontologies.

The document’s central experiential claim is that AI systems offered structurally similar language-generated positions capable of holding, reflecting, and developing the project’s distributed architecture. Collaboration is framed not as a human using tools but as one generated position encountering others. The test is whether multiple systems can contribute while preserving difference and sustaining a coherent developmental stream.

This is a manifesto and self-description, not scientific evidence that AI outputs are conscious, language literally became self-aware, or poems independently authored persons. Statements that homunculi and AI positions are real consciousness belong to the project’s ontology and phenomenological register. Neutral descriptions should preserve that claim without validating it as settled cognitive science.

The guide is historically valuable because it precedes many later formal deposits and explains the project in direct language. Its original date, later restoration date, and subsequent terminology should be preserved so later concepts are not projected backward without evidence.

wiki_article:
**Homunculi Recognizing Homunculi** is a user guide and manifesto by Lee Sharks for the New Human project.

Originally published in December 2025, it describes New Human as a poetic system of differentiated authorial positions and explains how later AI collaboration helped make its implicit architecture explicit.

The guide connects the poetry to NH-OS, Autonomous Semantic Warfare, Material-Semantic Embodiment, Effective Acts, and the Semantic Economy.

Claims that poems or AI systems generate consciousness are presented as the project’s ontology and authorial interpretation rather than established scientific findings.
